base_record_snapshot.lesson: A dehydration transform corrects the SOURCE surface's self-description and leaves the DESTINATION's self-description frozen at transform time — while the destination is precisely the surface that keeps accreting. Lived at tic 680: canonical/CLAUDE.md had its stale 'Pass-4-A draft / not yet swapped' banner corrected at /review 316, explicitly noted as having 'contradicted reality since the swap.' Its sibling and transform TARGET, constitution-ledger/ledger.md, never got the same correction: ledger.md:3 still reads 'Pass-4-B authored draft (tic 267)' and ledger.md:22 still reads 'Total demoted entries: 74' against 243 actual anchored entries — a 3.3x under-declaration, because ~169 entries were promoted INTO the ledger across tics 278-640 after the head was written. This is not covered by the existing structural-transform invariant, which enumerates the closed set of READERS OF THE SOURCE. The destination's own head-matter is a different locus: it is the transform's PRODUCT, and it degrades monotonically as the destination grows. It is a textbook silent-degrade consumer — an agent sizing the corpus from the head, or a rehydration lane budgeting a read, under-reads by 3.3x with no loud error — and it trips the internal-snapshots-must-carry-timestamps-or-TTLs invariant, the head being an unprobed tic-267 snapshot on the federation's largest doctrinal surface. The rule: a relocation's closed consumer set must include the DESTINATION's self-description, and any count in that self-description must be derived at read time or carry an explicit as-of tic.
